title: Resumable stream snapshotting and lease grace for interrupted tool invocations
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Context:
We observe two common failure modes during long-lived streaming generations with function/tool calls and structured outputs: (1) client disconnects or mobile app backgrounding causes partial drafts to be orphaned on the serving side, and (2) transient network flaps cause repeated retries that either duplicate tool invocations or drop partial tokens. Both scenarios increase cost, waste KV cache and backend resources, and produce poor UX since clients cannot resume an interrupted generation or reliably retrieve partial structured outputs/attachments.

Goal:
Introduce a resumable snapshot and lease-grace mechanism that: (a) captures lightweight resumable checkpoints for in-flight streaming generations (including KV cache fingerprints and tool-call idempotency tokens), (b) provides a short grace period during which a disconnected client can reconnect and resume, and (c) ensures safe cleanup of stale snapshots with tombstones to prevent accidental resumptions and duplicate tool invocations. Must remain backward compatible with older SDKs that do not support resume.

Design proposal (high-level):
1) Snapshot model: periodic lightweight snapshots (every N tokens or on function-call boundaries) that store: generation cursor, stable KV fingerprint, list of outstanding tool-call ids with idempotency tokens, and a small structured-output partial payload. Snapshots are versioned and linked by generation id. Snapshots are intended to be fast, small, and retrievable via a resume token returned to the client.

2) Lease and grace semantics: each generation has a short active lease (default 30s) renewed on normal heartbeats/pushes. On unexpected disconnect, the system keeps snapshots in a RECONNECT_GRACE window (configurable per-customer; default 5 minutes) before tombstoning. During grace, a returning client presenting the resume token can reconnect and continue. After grace expiration the snapshot is tombstoned and any outstanding tools are considered cancelled and their idempotency keys invalidated.

3) Tool/function-call safety: function calls that are "at-most-once" by default will be decorated with idempotency tokens. Resume will only re-issue tool calls when the snapshot indicates the call did not complete. If a tool provider cannot guarantee idempotency, the snapshot marks the call as non-resumable and forces an abort path with a clear client-facing status.

4) Compatibility shim: for SDKs without resume support, we will continue to honor snapshots server-side for the grace window but will not attempt automatic client resume. To avoid resource retention, we lower their grace window to a shorter TTL (default 60s) unless customer explicitly enables wider retention. We expose a header and dashboard metric to show SDK compatibility distribution.

5) Cleanup and tombstones: tombstones are applied atomically with any cancellation actions (release KV cache, revoke lease, mark idempotency tokens expired). Tombstones include a short audit trail entry for debugging. Periodic sweep job will compact old tombstones after retention (30d).

Acceptance criteria:
- Resume token issuance on all streaming starts and after each snapshot boundary.
- Reconnect flow: client reconnect within grace window and resumes token stream with preserved KV cache fingerprint and no duplication of completed function calls.
- If resume attempt occurs after tombstone, client receives a clear error code (RESUME_EXPIRED) and server performs safe cleanup.
- No increase in duplicated function-call invocations in e2e test matrix (see test plan).

Metrics and observability:
- New metrics: snapshot_size_bytes, snapshots_per_generation, resume_success_rate, resume_latency, orphaned_snapshots_count, tombstone_compactions_per_hour.
- Console dashboards: per-customer snapshot retention, SDK compatibility histogram, and cost impact estimate for orphaned snapshots.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable snapshotting and short grace (60s) for internal tenants and CI workloads. Run integration tests with simulated mobile disconnects and tool-call mocks.
Phase 2: opt-in for customers via console flag (30s->5min configurable). Expose SDK patch that supports resume token handling.
Phase 3: default-on for new generations; existing customers will be migrated with a 30-day notice and compatibility telemetry.

Testing:
- Unit tests for snapshot creation, serialization, and restoration.
- Integration tests that simulate disconnects at token, function-call start, and function-call return boundaries.
- Fault injection for idempotency token failure and partial commit races.
- Load test to measure snapshot creation overhead at high QPS.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Snapshot frequency vs latency/cost: more frequent snapshots improve resume granularity but increase cost and write amplification. Default N tokens = 64 for now; will tune based on telemetry.
- Data retention policy: customers in regulated environments may require longer grace windows; we must expose per-tenant controls and KMS scoping for snapshots.
- Interplay with existing garbage collection heuristics (batch-aware GC and lease revocation) needs a careful migration plan to avoid double-freeing KV entries.

Dependencies:
- Runtime kernel changes for efficient snapshot serialization (ENG-44610 referenced for lease-based ownership primitives).
- Console flagging and per-tenant configuration UI.

Security and compliance:
- Snapshots can include structured-output fragments that may contain PII. We will encrypt snapshots with tenant KMS keys when private deployment is enabled and add a redaction option for hosted mode. Requires security review.
